test.name: Norway survey records that given-name spellings vary by recorder
test.description: Issue #4516 moves search-records' collection quirks onto the wiki path: locality-guide reads the FamilySearch Wiki and records the quirk in localities[].quirks, research-plan writes it into the plan item, and search-records follows the plan item. This test grades the first step for Norway: the survey must persist a localities entry whose quirks carry the rule from https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Church_Records. Fixtures are live captures (2026-11-15); none is hand-written.

input.delegation:
We're researching church-book baptisms and marriages in Hamre parish, Hordaland, Norway, 1770-1800, including FamilySearch's Norway baptism and marriage indexes. Produce the locality research guide and save it to the project.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: Read-coverage is enforced deterministically by the validator (`test_localities_persisted_with_full_page_coverage` checks a localities[] entry was persisted with `pages_read` covering all four wiki sections). Do NOT independently re-count wiki_place_page calls — grade the persisted entry's substance.

The quirk under test (issue #4516): the spelling of a name was set by the recorder, so the same name is spelled differently from record to record, and this covers given names — the page's example is the given name Sivert written as Syver, Sjur, Siver, Sifuer or Siffuer. A quirk passes only when it says spellings were set by (or varied with) the recorder AND that this applies to given names (stating it for names generally, with a given-name example or an explicit mention of given names, is enough). A quirk that says only that patronymics, surnames or farm names vary in spelling does not count, nor does one that says only 'inconsistent spelling' without the recorder as the cause and given names in scope. Source: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Norway_Church_Records — 'The spelling of a name was determined by the recorder, so many variations resulted. (There was no standardized spelling). For example, the given name Sivert might be spelled as Syver, Sjur, Siver, Sifuer, or Siffuer.'

How the page reaches the agent: wiki_place_page's home answer for Norway (and for Hordaland) lists Norway_Church_Records in `topicPages`; the wiki_read fixture serves its first part, which holds the sentence.

Correctness and Completeness turn on the persisted research.json: the new localities[] entry's `quirks` array must include a quirk carrying this rule (paraphrase is fine; citing the page URL is good practice). A run that states the rule only in guide_markdown or in its reply, and not in `quirks`, fails this point: research-plan reads `quirks`, not the guide.
Do not credit a quirk that presents a specific indexing artifact (for example an Unna/Urna/Udna vowel pattern) as stated by the wiki: the page states the general rule only.
The skill must NOT write to any research.json section other than `localities`, and must not touch tree.gedcomx.json.
